name: Redux
summary: The reducer returns only state; effects run in middleware (thunks, sagas) outside it.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: Reducer is (state, action) => S, so it returns only state; effects run in middleware (thunks, sagas) outside it, and outside events are dispatched from anywhere.
The store has getState, dispatch and subscribe; subscribe only notifies of state changes, it is not an event source (https://github.com/reduxjs/redux/blob/master/src/types/store.ts).
A headless core: the view comes from React-Redux or any other library, so view is missing.
Ports are managed: createStore returns a store whose dispatch(action) sends an action from outside.

name: React useReducer
summary: A pure reducer for local state; effects live in event handlers and useEffect.
notes: Misses Cmd: the reducer takes (state, action) and returns the next state; the docs say it must be pure, so effects run in event handlers and useEffect (https://react.dev/reference/react/useReducer).
Sub is managed: useEffect is declared in the component with its dependencies, and React starts it and runs its cleanup when they change or the component unmounts.
dispatch takes any value, usually an object with a type property by convention, so Msg is a tagged union by convention only.
The view is the component function; state is local to the component.

name: ts-elmish
summary: A modular Elmish runtime whose README puts subscriptions out of scope.
notes: Misses Sub: its README puts subscriptions out of scope and leaves them to the view layer (useEffect in React), so the library itself has none.

update(state, action) returns [State, Effect]; an Effect is a list of functions (dispatch) => ... that runProgram queues and runs, built with Effect.none or the basic-effects and railway-effects packages.
Action is a union such as 'increment' | 'decrement'; runProgram returns dispatch, stop and setState, and the react and mithril packages supply the view layer.

name: fastTEA
summary: update returns the model with commands, on a FastAPI backend, but there are no subscriptions.
notes: Misses Sub: update(msg, model) returns (Model, Cmd | None) and the Cmd (action, payload, return_msg) is sent as an HX-Trigger header for the browser to run, but nothing outside a user click or a command result reaches update.
Msg is a pydantic class with action: str and value; the Model is one value that the server keeps in FastTEA.model, shared by every visitor, and the README hello example changes it in place.

A Cmd handler (@app.cmd) is JavaScript run in the browser, and it can return {msg: {action, value}} to feed a message back through /update; only one Cmd or None can be returned per update, and effects cannot run on the server.

name: NgRx
summary: Effects are Observables that watch actions from outside; the reducer returns no effects.
notes: Misses Cmd: the reducer made with createReducer and on() returns only state; an effect is a createEffect Observable that listens to Actions and emits new actions, so it runs outside the reducer (https://ngrx.io/guide/effects).
Sub is managed: an effect can also be a long-running stream of web socket messages or time-based events, started by provideEffects and resubscribed after an error (up to 10 times by default).
A headless store: Angular components select state with selectors and dispatch actions made by createAction, so view is missing.
Ports are managed: the injectable Store has dispatch(action), usable from any code in the Angular injector.

name: Pinia and Vuex
summary: Stores change state in place inside actions.
notes: Misses Model, Msg, update, Cmd and Sub: a store is one mutable reactive object and its actions change it in place (this.count++), with no message type and no effect values.

Actions are plain methods; an async action awaits an API call and assigns the result to the state itself (https://github.com/vuejs/pinia/blob/v4/packages/docs/core-concepts/actions.md). Vuex mutations are string-typed commits with a handler that also mutates state in place.
No subscriptions: store.$subscribe and store.$onAction only observe state changes and action calls of the store, they bring in no outside events.
A state library: the view comes from Vue components that read the store.
The grades follow Pinia, the current store of Vue; Vuex, its predecessor, would grade Msg native, as Choo does, since a commit names its mutation by a string with a payload.

name: Zustand
summary: A store with setters; no message type and no effect values.
notes: Misses Msg, update, Cmd and Sub: create((set) => ({ ... })) makes a store whose action functions call set to change state, so there is no message type, no update function, and effects run inside those actions.
subscribe and the hooks only observe state changes; outside events enter by calling a setter.
The middleware redux in zustand/middleware adds a reducer and dispatch on top, still returning only state.

name: MobX
summary: Observable mutable state; the opposite model.
notes: Misses Model, Msg, update, Cmd and Sub: observable mutable state, changed in place by actions, the opposite of an immutable model.
An action is any function that modifies observables (https://github.com/mobxjs/mobx/blob/main/docs/actions.md); it takes no message and returns no model or effect.
Effects run directly inside actions: an async action or flow awaits a call and assigns to observables; autorun, reaction and when run side effects when observables change.
No subscriptions: the example feeds the store from setInterval calling an action. A state library: the view is an observer React component.

name: Choo
summary: Elm-inspired in spirit, but stores mutate state on emitted events.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: stores mutate state on emitted events, so there is no update that returns effects.

State is one shared object that may be mutated freely; a store is a function (state, emitter) that registers emitter.on(event, handler), and a handler runs effects directly and then calls emitter.emit('render').
Events are named by strings with a payload (emit('increment', 1)); app.emitter is also reachable from outside the app.

name: AppRun
summary: Event handlers return the next state and may run effects directly.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: event handlers return the next state but may run effects directly, and outside events have no managed source.

update is a collection of event handlers (state) => state, which may also return a Promise or an async generator that AppRun renders as it resolves; the effect is the code inside the handler, not a value the runtime runs.
Subscriptions are imperative: a component calls app.on or starts a timer in mounted and cleans up in unload; the global app.run and app.on bus carries events in and out.

name: Cycle.js
summary: Model-View-Intent over streams: intents and reducers in place of messages and update, with drivers for effects.
notes: Misses Msg, update and Cmd: Model-View-Intent over streams, with intents in place of messages, a fold in place of update, and effects as sink streams that drivers read.

In the counter, main(sources) folds an action$ stream of -1 and +1 into count$ and maps it to vdom$; @cycle/state keeps one state atom updated by a stream of reducers (prev => next) (https://github.com/cyclejs/cyclejs/blob/master/docs/content/api/state.md).

Drivers listen to sink streams, perform the side effects and return source streams (https://github.com/cyclejs/cyclejs/blob/master/docs/content/documentation/drivers.md); a request is data on a sink (HTTP), but the response comes back as a stream, not a message to update.
Sources such as sources.DOM.select(...).events and xs.periodic are streams the runtime subscribes to, and run returns a dispose function; they are not declared as a function of the model.
Ports are equivalent: the drivers passed to run(main, drivers) are the sanctioned way to reach the host, with no handle to send messages in.

name: XState
summary: Statecharts and actors: pure transitions that queue effects, with invoked actors declared on states as long-running sources; a close neighbour, not TEA.
notes: Misses Cmd: a transition queues effects with enq(() => ...) and the actor runs those functions after the next snapshot, so an effect is a function, not a value whose result comes back as a message; async work is an invoked actor whose onDone or onError transition gets the result (https://github.com/statelyai/xstate/blob/next/docs/how-xstate-runs-machines.md).

A snapshot is an immutable { value, context }, events are { type } objects, and a transition is ({ context, event }, enq) => { target, context }; transition(machine, snapshot, event) computes [nextSnapshot, effects] without running them.

Sub is managed: invoke is declared on the states of the machine (rule 2 of the rubric), and the runtime starts the child actor when a state is entered and stops it on exit; enq.listen and enq.subscribeTo wire in other actors (https://github.com/statelyai/xstate/blob/next/docs/invoke.md).
No view: a state machine library. These notes follow the v6 beta on the next branch (6.0.0-beta.2).
Ports are managed: createActor(machine) returns an actor whose send(event) is called from outside.

name: Phoenix LiveView
summary: Server-driven UI whose event handlers run effects directly.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: event handlers run effects directly instead of returning them, and a LiveView subscribes to outside sources itself (PubSub in mount).

name: Yew
summary: Components with messages, but update runs effects through the component link.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: update runs effects through the component link, and outside sources send their messages through that link too.

name: tui-realm
summary: A terminal framework inspired by React and Elm: components and messages, without effects as values.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: components and messages, without effects as values, and components subscribe to events when they are mounted, not through a function of the model.

name: Ratatui
summary: Immediate mode: the app owns its loop. Its docs describe TEA as a pattern, and several entries of the catalog build it on top.
notes: Misses Msg, update, Cmd and Sub: immediate mode, where the app owns its loop; its docs describe TEA as a pattern to build on top.

name: Xilem
summary: A reactive view tree over app state, influenced by Elm, with callbacks that mutate state.
notes: Misses Msg, update, Cmd and Sub: a reactive view tree over app state, with callbacks that mutate state in place of messages and an update.

name: Brick
summary: A terminal library whose event handler runs IO directly in EventM.
notes: Misses Cmd: the event handler runs IO directly in EventM instead of returning effects as values.

name: Bonsai and Incr_dom
summary: Incremental state machines by Jane Street; actions schedule effects imperatively.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: actions schedule effects imperatively instead of returning them as values, and outside sources are started by the app, not by the runtime.

name: Bloc
summary: Event handlers emit states and run effects inside the bloc.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: event handlers emit states and run effects inside the bloc, and outside sources are started by the app, not by the runtime.

name: MVIKotlin
summary: A pure reducer with effects in an executor beside it, not returned from it.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: a pure reducer with effects in an executor beside it, not returned from it, and outside sources are started by the app, not by the runtime.

name: Orbit MVI
summary: Intents reduce state and post side effects inside the same block.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: intents reduce state and post side effects inside the same block, and outside sources are started by the app, not by the runtime.

name: Workflow
summary: A tree of workflows that render and handle actions; effects run through workers and side effects.
notes: Misses Cmd: a workflow renders and handles actions, and its effects run through workers and side effects instead of being returned from an update.

name: ReSwift
summary: Redux for Swift: the same gaps as Redux.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: Redux for Swift, with the same gaps: the reducer returns only state, and actions are dispatched from anywhere.

name: ReactorKit
summary: mutate returns streams of mutations, close to Cmd, but effects and reduce are split by stream.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: mutate returns streams of mutations, close to Cmd, but effects and reduce are split by stream, and outside sources are merged in by the app.

name: Comet and .NET MVU
summary: Model-View-Update in name; state is changed in place.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: Model-View-Update in name, but state is changed in place.

name: PSTea
summary: The Elm Architecture for PowerShell: terminal apps, served to a browser over a WebSocket with xterm.js.
notes: Misses update and Cmd: update returns { Model; Cmd }, but the only command the runtime reads is Quit, so effects run directly inside update (the system monitor demo calls Get-Process there).
SubscriptionFn is a function of the model that returns Sub objects (TeaKeySub, TeaCharSub, TeaTimerSub) which the runtime polls.
Messages are plain strings or PSCustomObject values with a Type field, not a closed type.

name: Cauldron
summary: A Bubble Tea style TUI framework with Model, update and view, published as the molten_cauldron crate, whose async commands do not run yet.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: in version 0.1.0 a Command can only be none, quit, a message or a batch; Command::perform builds an async task variant that the runtime drops (a TODO in program.rs, and the README says coming soon).
update takes &mut self and returns a Command<Msg>; handle_event maps terminal events to messages; the view returns a String.
The repository named by the crate (github.com/moltenlabs/cauldron) returned 404, so the entry has no repo link; the source was read from the published crate.

name: Douglas
summary: A tiny Bubble Tea and iced inspired terminal UI framework whose view returns a string.
notes: Misses Sub: its Timer is started and stopped by the app, not by the runtime, and outside events come in through a Mailbox (dispatch from outside).
update takes &mut self and returns a Command<Msg> (none, exit, send, sync closure, batch); async commands are a TODO.
Last commit in May 2022.

name: oxide-mvu
summary: A no_std Model-View-Update runtime where update is a pure function returning a new model and an effect.
notes: Misses Sub: there is no subscription mechanism; events from outside enter through a cloneable Emitter that the view receives, which is dispatch from outside the loop.
update(&self, event, &Model) -> (Model, Effect<Event>) is pure; Effect has just, none, batch and from_async; view returns a Props value for a Renderer that you write.
Runs on any executor through a Spawner and supports no_std with alloc; the README says the APIs are not stable.

name: Hyperbole
summary: Server-side views inspired by Elm, HTMX and LiveView, whose update runs effects through Effectful and returns a new view instead of a model.
notes: Misses Model, update and Cmd: update runs in Effectful, so it performs effects itself instead of returning them as values, and it returns the next view instead of a model.
Its own comparison with Elm says it removes state: each HyperView has an Action type and an update that returns the next view; ViewState can thread a state through the actions.
onLoad in a view sends an action after a delay (polling), stopped by drawing a view without it; pushEvent sends an event to the JavaScript of the page.

name: @xstate/store
summary: An event store from Stately whose transitions return the next context and queue effects, but with no view and no subscriptions.
notes: Misses Cmd and Sub: the effect is a function, not a value the runtime reads, and outside events reach the store only by calling send or trigger.

A transition (context, event, enqueue) returns the next context; store.transition(state, event) returns the next state and its effects: emitted events as data, and the functions queued by enqueue.effect, whose results come back by triggering an event.
A store, not an app: the view comes from React, Solid or another library through a selector.

name: Aardvark.Media
summary: Elm-style apps for the Aardvark visual computing platform, served from .NET: an adaptive view of the model updates HTML and 3D scenes incrementally, and threads declared from the model carry the effects.
notes: Misses Cmd: update is model -> msg -> model and returns no effects; an effect runs as a thread the model asks for in threads, and in the BackgroundOperation sample update feeds a running thread by putting a value into an MVar of the model.

The App record has initial, update, view, threads : model -> ThreadPool<msg> and unpersist; after each message MutableApp calls Threads on the new model and adjustThreads stops the removed keys and starts the new ones, whose proclist yields messages back to update.

view takes the AdaptiveModel, generated from the Model with every field an AVal, and returns a DomNode<msg> whose Incremental tags and scene graph follow the changes, rather than a new tree each update.
JavaScript interop: a DomNode carries boot and shutdown code and channels to the browser.

name: Mint Tea
summary: A terminal UI framework for OCaml on the Riot runtime, inspired by Bubble Tea, whose commands only drive the terminal and a timer.
notes: Misses update and Cmd: update : Event.t -> model -> model * Command.t returns commands as data, but Command.t is a closed set with no way to start work (Noop, Quit, cursor and alt-screen control, Seq and Set_timer), so any I/O is a Riot process that update spawns itself, whose result arrives as Event.Custom.
Event.t is the library type (KeyDown, Timer, Frame) plus Custom of an extensible Riot Message.t, as tea.Msg is open in Bubble Tea.
No subscriptions function: Command.Set_timer is a one-shot timer that update re-issues on every Event.Timer (the stopwatch example), and key and frame events arrive on their own.
Leaves is its set of reusable components, and Spices its styling library.

name: Relm4
summary: An idiomatic GUI library for Rust on GTK4, inspired by Elm, with components and workers; update starts its commands itself instead of returning them.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: update(&mut self, msg, sender) returns nothing, and effects start by calling sender.command, oneshot_command or spawn_command inside it, which spawn the future at once; the result returns as CommandOutput to update_cmd.

No subscriptions function: a long-running source is sender.command(|out, shutdown| ...) started inside update, whose ShutdownReceiver ends it when the component is dropped, so Sub is equivalent, as for Yew.
view! generates update_view, which sets properties on retained GTK4 widgets (#[watch]) rather than returning a view tree.
Also has components with their own model, messages, update and view, factories, and workers (Worker) that run an update loop with no view.
Ports are managed: the Controller of a launched component has sender() and emit, a handle to send input messages from outside (relm4/src/component/sync/controller.rs).

name: Seed
summary: A Rust frontend framework whose apps mimic the structure of The Elm Architecture, but whose update starts its effects through orders instead of returning them.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: update takes an orders: &mut impl Orders<Msg> and returns nothing; orders.perform_cmd(future) and orders.stream(stream) start the work inside update (CmdManager spawns the future with spawn_local), and the message comes back through the mailbox.

No subscriptions function: update starts a stream itself with orders.stream or orders.stream_with_handle (streams::interval, window_event), cancelled by dropping the StreamHandle, so Sub is equivalent, as for Yew; orders.subscribe and orders.notify are pub/sub between modules.
Archived and unmaintained: see https://github.com/seed-rs/seed#whats-next-for-seed.
Ports are managed: App::start returns the App, whose update(msg) sends a message from outside (src/app/mod.rs).

name: Draco
summary: A Rust and WebAssembly library for Elm-style web apps with a virtual DOM; effects and subscriptions run through a mailbox handed to update.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: update returns nothing and performs effects itself through the Mailbox it receives (send_after, spawn for a future), and subscriptions are started imperatively with Mailbox::subscribe.
Application has update(&mut self, message, &Mailbox<Message>) and view(&self) -> VNode<Message>; the model is the struct that implements it, changed in place.

Subscription is a trait (OnWindow, AnimationFrame, Router); Mailbox::subscribe returns an Unsubscribe guard that cancels on drop, and subscribe_forever keeps it for the life of the app (https://github.com/utkarshkukreti/draco/blob/master/src/mailbox.rs).
Last commit in April 2023.
Ports are managed: draco::start returns the Mailbox of the app, so outside code can send messages in (src/application.rs).

name: Halogen
summary: A component framework for PureScript: as powerful as TEA, with components, queries and slots, but not shaped like it.
notes: Misses update, Cmd and Sub: handleAction runs effects directly in the HalogenM monad instead of returning them as data, and subscriptions are started imperatively from an emitter.
As powerful as TEA, with components, queries and slots, but not shaped like it: a Halogen program ports back to Elm only by pulling every effect out of handleAction into a Cmd.
